objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, please continue.', approving PHASE-HALO-20261103-001's recommendation): which faces a handle uses. Classify opened handles by the faces around the attachment point that they create through (their own faces or the opposite ones), explain the Fano plane against census 58 through the handle's port relation after a removal and the merged face of the split, and prove the opposite-face law for the handles that obey it. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-03: successful, with a corrected law. Each face around the attachment point reads one bit of the handle, whether two ports agree (reading lemma), and a frozen line can claim an own arc from one port pattern but an opposite face from two (claim lemma). An opened handle creates at a frozen line exactly when a pair of its points freezes it and neither point alone excludes either claim (claim rule: route direction proved, converse computed with no disagreement). Across a census of 305 handles the faces used are a property of the handle's port relation; the Fano plane never uses an own arc because each of its single points removes one pattern per other class. The PHASE-HALO law of the faces around the point is false: at a junction of a ladder arm spliced onto a grid the frozen region runs along the arm and every handle tested creates there, exactly confirmed on a small piece. Next: the frozen region by heights, and rigid strips (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the faces each census handle uses are classified by a stated rule, checked against exact creation, and the opposite-face law is proved for the handles that obey it or a counterexample is recorded.
